newsitem.title: USA: Stocks move lower as market looks to Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks move lower as market looks to Fed meeting.

text.p: Stocks fell in cautious trading Tuesday as investors awaited the outcome of a meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers to set the course of interest rates.

Even once the central bank's meeting -- widely expected to produce no change in rates -- was out of the way, investors should continue to hang back ahead of Friday's key January job report, analysts said.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 28.48 points at 6,777.68. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 11-8 on volume of 275 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index lost 10.70 to 1,365.35, and the American Stock Exchange index was off 0.60 at 589.11.
The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee started a two-day meeting Tuesday to decide whether to change interest rates.
Although the consensus is that the Fed will hold the line on interest rates when the meeting ends on Wednesday, investors were sidelined because a Fed meeting is always cause for some caution.

"Everybody is in limbo until the Fed meeting ends. There are a couple of analyst who think rates may be raised, and no one wants to get on the wrong side of the Fed," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury was unchanged and its yield held at Monday's close of 6.74 percent.

The computer networking sector took a beating after Xylan Corp. reported fourth quarter earnings that were below analysts' expectations, and 3Com Corp. fell prey to renewed fears of a repeat of the sales slowdown seen in December.
Xylan plunged 7-7/8 at 20-5/8 and 3Com tumbled 6-1/2 to 55-3/8.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell cut earnings estimates on both Xylan and 3Com.
Elsewhere, International Business Machines lost 3-3/8 to 151-1/2, and Cisco Systems was down 3 at 65-1/4.
